articleTitle: ASIC Circuit Netlist Recognition Using Graph Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Circuit netlist recognition is an important step in the analysis flow of hardware assurance. The main objective in circuit netlist recognition is to classify circuit netlists into different categories according to their structural differences for the purposes of design verification and trojan detection. Traditional methods are usually based on human knowledge and statistical heuristics, which incur a large degree of error and cannot easily handle large ASIC circuit netlists. In this paper, we propose a machine learning solution based on graph neural network for automated circuit classification. By performing experiments on example synthesized ASIC circuits, we showed that our machine learning model produces highly accurate predictions of 98.3% accuracy.

articleTitle: The Failure Mechansim of the E-SOA Boundary of Power Transistor Collapsed at Higher Gate Voltage
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The ID-VD curves of the power transistor for the boundary extraction of the electrical safe-operating area (E-SOA) are often measured by the hundred-nanosecond pulse (TLP) to differentiate it from the thermal SOA. However, the E-SOA boundary collapse at the low gate voltage is still caused by the thermal. It is the Joule-heating lowering the turn-on threshold voltage of bipolar as temperature increases. For the high gate voltage, the E-SOA boundary collapse is caused by the TLP induced magnetic-field at the transistor turn-on transient, which leads to the current crowding effect as well as source-drain short effect. From the electromagnetic simulations, the two effects are demonstrated as the electrons of the channels exerted by the Lozentz force flow outside the channels to fill whole regions of the finger edges of transistor under the time-varying magnetic field created by the time-varying current.

articleTitle: Low-voltage EBIC investigation of fails
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: An investigation of shorting defects in SRAM structures by means of low-voltage EBIC is presented and the location of the defect was compared to the one isolated with EBIRCH. A pulldown device in 7 nm technology was intentionally overstressed, and the shorting location isolated with EBIRCH at 500 V. Then a series of EBIC investigations at very low voltage were undertaken in an experiment to isolate the problem. It was determined that some information about the nature of the defect was clear at beam landing energies as low as 150 eV.

articleTitle: Simultaneous, Submicron Infrared and Raman Microspectroscopies for Effective Failure and Contamination Analyses
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: We demonstrate the analysis of ~1 µm contamination with high signal-to-noise in a simultaneous infrared and Raman microscope at the same time, at the same location and at submicron spatial resolution. This combined technique provides high sensitivity to small sample volumes without melting or damaging the samples by using separate infrared excitation and visible laser detection mechanisms. The measurement process does not involve physically contacting the sample, hence simplifying sample preparation and avoiding cross-contamination between sample changes. To showcase this new capability, we provide examples from the contamination in the gap between a solder joint and a non-wetting pad, adhesive residues on a glass panel and foreign matter near a copper post. Such challenges could not be readily resolved with conventional FTIR and Raman techniques. The simultaneous O-PTIR and Raman brings complementary and confirmatory results to analysis previously thought to be difficult to impossible.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Negative Bias Temperature Instability Model for Gallium-nitride Metal-insulator-semiconductor High Electron Mobility Transistors From 77K to 393K
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This work studies the degradation mechanisms behind negative bias temperature instability (NBTI) in galliumnitride metal-insulator semiconductor high electron mobility transistors (GaN MIS-HEMT) under a wide range of temperature conditions (77K to 393K). The positive shift of threshold voltage increases with temperature from 77K to 303K, owing to the trapping of electrons in the silicon nitride (Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) bulk layer and at the Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>/aluminum gallium nitride (AlGaN) interface. Anomalously, the threshold voltage shift substantially reduces from 303K to 393K. Such an abnormal phenomenon could be attributed to additional hole trapping in Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> due to impact ionization. The occurrence of impact ionization can be further evidenced by the recovery behavior if the test devices. Accordingly, a comprehensive model is proposed to clarify the degradation behavior of NBTI for GaN MIS-HEMT under different temperature conditions.

articleTitle: Electromigration of Gold Metallization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This study investigates the electromigration performance of gold metallization with vias of different sizes and shapes. Electromigration lifetime was limited by void formation which scaled directly with via size, especially those with square vias, where the fatal void formed in the via at the interface of the feeder metal. This dependence saturates for larger vias once the failure mode switches to voiding through the thickness of the tested metal at the cathode line-end. The highest lifetimes were measured for line-only structures where failure was observed at the grain boundaries. Further, non-square vias can be mapped to an equivalent square via size to enable electromigration design rule formulation. Also, the activation energy and current-density exponent as seen in Black’s Law were measured to be 0.41eV and n = 2.14, respectively, on structures with vias, which indicates low temperature dependence and void-nucleation limited failure. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Dynamic Defect Localization by Toggling Integrated Circuits States
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: the article demonstrates obtaining useful dynamic fault localization results by toggling integrated circuits (IC) between different modes. Compared with a static stimulus setting, a dynamic setup provides the opportunity to detect the transition state of the faulty circuit during the switching between modes enabling better fault localization.

articleTitle: A Reliability-Concerned Compute-in-Memory Behavior Model for Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: A reliability-concerned compute-in-memory (CIM) behavior model is developed to evaluate and optimize the performance of convolutional neural network (CNN), like LeNet, VGG. Non-ideal factors, such as cell delay variation and mismatch are concerned as parameters in image classification tasks. The inference accuracy will be evaluated under specific dataset, neural network architecture, mapping method with non-ideal factors. In this work, a quantized CNN is designed for image classification as a case study to show how to perform circuit-algorithm evaluation with the developed reliability-concerned CIM behavior model. The accuracy of the quantized neural network for MNIST achieves 97% with variation=0.1 in Gaussian distribution.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Discharge Switch Simulation Enablement in RF SOI Technologies
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: High current simulation capability under electrostatic discharge (ESD) conditions for ESD self-protected front end module (FEM) switch applications in an RF SOI Technology is shown for the first time. A methodology showing how to adequately characterize CMOS switch devices under ESD conditions is reviewed. Additionally, a methodology for extraction of a high current compact wrapper model which includes the parasitic bipolar transistor placed in parallel with the base MOSFET compact model is shown. Successful compact model simulation to hardware correlation is shown under ESD stress events.

articleTitle: HV ESD Device Solution Evaluations in 55nm BCD Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Effective High-Voltage (HV) ESD (Electrostatic Discharge) solutions for 12V power pad protection in 55nm BCDLite® were studied in this paper. A comparison between different types of devices, gate-grounded NMOS (GGNMOS), PNP, and NPN for HV ESD protection with key performance metrics were studied.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis using Advanced Modeling Technique for MEMS Microphone
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive failure analysis on a MEMS microphone and an innovative design approach to improve reliability performance. Finite element simulation and lumped parameter circuit modeling approaches are used to validate physical testing. We identify the critical back cavity volume and front volume etched cavity surface imperfections which primarily govern the failure mechanism. Strong dependence of the back cavity volume on the microphone reliability has been discovered for a given diaphragm thickness. The failure mechanism observed is the shattering of the diaphragm with the back-plate structure still intact. With the novel X-rib front volume etched cavity design, we succeeded in improving the reliability performance by more than 50% of the failure pressure, with the diaphragm and the back plate structure still remaining robust.

articleTitle: Case Studies: Masked read-only memory failure fault isolation without bitmapping
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Masked Read-Only Memory (MROM) is one type of non-volatile memory in which the content of the memory is pre-programmed during the manufacturing process. Its simplistic design of hard-wiring on bit line and source line makes it a cost-effective choice as compared to other Non-Volatile Memories (NVM) in System-On-Chip (SOC). However, the main drawback in such design lies in the lack of the diagnostic options for fault isolation. This paper presents the challenges and discusses the effective of dynamic electrical failure analysis techniques in debugging MROM.

articleTitle: A new 3D X-ray solution for non-destructive construction analysis of advanced electronics packages
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Over the last decade, 3D X-ray has become essential for non-destructive construction analysis of semiconductor packages [1]–[6]. This analysis is often done by skilled technicians using advanced X-ray systems. A recent trend in advanced IC package solutions is for a significant increase in 3D complexity and interconnect density [7]–[9]. These advanced package solutions are pushing the detection capabilities of existing X-ray systems, as well the analytical capabilities of the technicians who interpret the results [10]–[11]. In order to keep-up with industry requirements, an X-ray solution is developed to break through these performance barriers. In this article a new semi-automated workflow for 3D measurement of sub-surface interconnects in complex 3D IC packages will be described. This workflow is based on newly developed X-ray hardware and a semi-automated data analytics system which extracts actionable data from package interconnects. A commercial 3D DRAM package will be analyzed using the proposed workflow and data will be extracted which would be difficult or impractical to obtain using legacy methodologies, whether destructive or not. The reliability and repeatability of the proposed workflow will be tested and validated on multiple samples by measuring the critical dimensions repeatedly over a six-month period.

articleTitle: Significance of Dynamic Electrical Fault Isolation Techniques on buried Via Void defects
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Buried voids located underneath metal has always been a challenge to detect. In this work, we discuss the significance of dynamic electrical fault isolation techniques on buried via void that inaccessible by simple chip power-up. A buried void-induced functional hard fail case study and an ATPG soft fail case study will be demonstrated.

articleTitle: HCI SOA Enhancement for EDNMOS with Metal Field Plate
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This paper discusses Hot-Carrier Injection (HCI) for extended-drain nMOSFET (EDNMOS) with Metal Field Plate (MFP). The HCI linear-region drain current degradation is compared between a typical EDNMOS with MFP, and a typical EDNMOS without MFP. The difference in HCI linear-region drain current degradation is described using Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) simulations that show the magnitude of the electric field and impact ionization at the drain to gate edge region. Additionally, the HCI Safe-Operating Area (SOA) is simulated from the Aging HCI silicon data using an AgeMOS model. It is shown from the HCI SOA that there are improvements in the HCI reliability operating boundary for the EDNMOS with MFP as compared to the EDNMOS without MFP, especially in the switch (i.e. high V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> and low V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>) region.

articleTitle: Atmospheric corrosion of Ag/Cu plated FeNi based leadframe used in MOSFET package
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Environmental conditions, such as humidity, temperature, corrosive gas, play a significant effect on the reliability and lifetime of electronic packages. Presence of small amount of hydrogen sulphide (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S), even at ppb level, could bring severe problems in electronics. The most susceptible materials to H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S should be silver (Ag) and copper (Cu), as H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S will corrode these metals and form sulfides, especially with the presence of humidity.In this paper, a type of molded MOSFET package (Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor) encountered electricity opening in the field after about one year’s service. Failure analysis located the failure area was the leadframe, and subsequent cross-section showed the leadframe was severely corroded from the package edge to inside. This is an Ag and Cu plated FeNi based leadframe (5μm Ag/5μm Cu/NiFe based). Physical failure analysis and surface analysis were employed to characterize the leadframe failure mechanism. The corrosion mechanism of Ag/Cu plated FeNi based leadframe was studied in details. It was found that the Ag plating layer which close to the device edge was almost corroded, whilst the Cu layer underneath it was slightly corroded. The NiFe base was intact. However, it is interesting to found that there was no silver sulphide (AgS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) corrosion compound detected in the Ag layer. On the other hand, there was copper sulphide (CuS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) detected.It is suggested that this was a sulphur originated corrosion of leadframe. The MOSFET molded device served close to the coal-generation power plants, where the environmental gas contained high level sulphur (like H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S). The gas penetrated into the molded device through the leadframe and molded compound interface. S attacked the leadframe top layers Ag and Cu. Because Ag ions were inclined to migrate, the Ag ions migrated via the lead surface to the external leads, and accumulated at the lead at the package edge. On the other hand, Cu ions transported away from its original sites and eventually deposited on the cathodic areas as Cu salts, i.e. CuS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> which was detected by EDX and AES.

articleTitle: Failure Localization of Bipolar Integrated Circuits by Implementing Active Voltage Contrast
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Bipolar ICs are playing an important role in military applications, mainly used in logic gates, such as inverter and NAND gate. A metal break defect located on the step is one of the main failure mechanisms of bipolar ICs, resulting in open-circuit or functional failure. In this situation, general failure localization methods like optical beam induced resistance change (OBIRCH) and photon emission microscopy (PEM) might not be fully effective. However, active voltage contrast (AVC) can be used as a voltage probe, which may pinpoint the incorrect potential and thus locate the failure position. Two case studies will be present in this paper on how to implement AVC for failure localization, and the detailed failure mechanism will be discussed.

articleTitle: Influence of RPO Film and CESL Material on Data Retention in Non-Volatile Memory
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: in this study, we evaluated the effect of resist protection oxide (RPO) and contact etch stop layer (CESL) on the retention characteristics of non-volatile memory (NVM). Based on this comprehensive study, though thicker RPO thickness and NH3-based silicon nitride (SiN) CESL can improve data retention, few samples suffer unexpected large variation issues. These retention behaviors result in unstable data storage performance and potentially lead to product failures and production yield loss. An alternative solution has been explored to improve the data retention characteristic by replacing the NH3-based CESL with N2-based mixing NH3 gas flow. This method successfully demonstrates excellent data retention capability in the actual memory samples.

articleTitle: SIMS Analysis of Ultra-Shallow Boron Implant
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry is a well-known technique that is widely used for characterization of implant profile in semiconductor industry. Due to the continuous transistor scaling, the junction depth has reduced to less than 5nm and the characterization of the implant profile becomes ever challenging due to the SIMS transient region effect. In this paper, SIMS analysis of the shallow boron implant showed different observation from the conventional way that the effect of primary ion energy to the surface transient effect.

articleTitle: Automatic Defect Review of a Patterned Wafer using Hybrid Metrology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The scaling trend toward under 5nm in semiconductor design requires tighter control over defects on wafers. To measure defects on wafer surfaces, several kinds of inspection and review tools can be employed—i.e., Surface Scanning Inspection Systems (SSIS), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), or Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM). Among the options, Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) has proven particularly advantageous because it directly measures the dimensions (height and width) and physical properties of defects of interest and gives reference information for other characterization tools. At the same time, since the AFM measurement speed is relatively slow, it is unrealistic to find all defects on the wafer surface by using AFM alone. Therefore, we have introduced the hybrid metrological instrument by combining White Light Interferometer (WLI) to an industrial automated AFM platform. By utilizing the vibration-isolated platform and the low noise z scanner of AFM, the performance of WLI has significantly been improved, achieving unprecedented high z resolution. We introduce a method to identify the differences between wafers to locate the hot spots quickly and investigate the problems, thereby measuring many minor defects on the patterned wafer with higher throughput. The hybridization of WLI and AFM provides us new possibilities in semiconductor and other industrial applications.

articleTitle: Finding Invisible Cracks via Nano-Probing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Nano-probing is a failure analysis technique widely discussed in recent years. As semiconductor features continually shrink, conventional emission tools become increasingly challenged in localizing the failure site to a single transistor level. Therefore, nano-probing becomes essential in further isolating the failing transistor in order to reveal the physical defect. In this paper, we will show a case study of utilizing a nano-probing tool to isolate the exact failing location where an embedded crack causes a circuity failure. We also analyze the crack with Focused-Ion-Beam (FIB) cross-section and Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy (STEM) elemental mapping to obtain more detailed information about the defect.

articleTitle: Analysis for the Physical Mechanism of the Abnormal Increase of Idsat in NMOS under HCI
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Generally speaking, when NMOS is stressed at I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bmax</inf>, its I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf> will decrease due to electrons injecting into the oxide [1]-[2]. However, we found that the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf> under HCI stress at I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bmax</inf> will first increase and then decrease, it is similar to the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf> mentioned in other papers [3]-[4], it decreases first, increases in the middle before finally decreasing. We conducted experiments to find possible root causes, such as LDD concentration change, LDD angle of incidence change, and ambient temperature change. The results show that with the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf> increase, the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> also showed an increase, but the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dlin</inf> decreased. The results also reveal that the more severe the HCI, such as low temperature, lower LDD concentration, and a small LDD angle of incidence, the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf> of NMOS during HCI stress will increase obviously due to more increase in I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>. So we concluded that the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> originated from a junction leakage between drain(n+) and LDD(n-), and it increases with HCI stress, but it will be saturated after a amount of time, when the hot electrons from HC impact continue to be injected into the oxide, it will make the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf> to exhibit a turn-around. Finally, the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> curve keeps the MOSFET characteristics, but its saturated current is much smaller than that of I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>, this indirectly confirms that the abnormal increase in I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf> is strongly related to I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> and a lot of hot electrons have injected into the oxide. As for the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dlin</inf> measured by small V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> always decreases, the leakage current can be neglected because the reverse bias of the junction is small.

articleTitle: Innovative use of TCAD Process Simulation for Device Failure Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The complex 3D structure of FinFET device has posed new challenges for Physical Failure Analysis (PFA) since its introduction in the 22nm technology node. FinFET process is complicated which could translate into different variation of defects in the device. This will inadvertently make it challenging to pinpoint the exact process step where the defect was introduced. Through TCAD process simulation, a digital twin of the actual device can be created based on actual layout and process, from which the defect formation mechanism can be identified. In this work, we showcase the innovative use of Sentaurus Process Explorer (SPX) TCAD simulation to produce a structurally accurate FinFET process model that could model real-life defective FinFET device to gain useful insight during failure analysis.

articleTitle: A Novel CMOS Image Sensor Package Cover Glass White Stain Material Identification Metrology by TOF-SIMS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The demand of CMOS Image Sensor (CIS) in consumer electronics and automotive industries is increasing from day to day in the era of Internet of Things (IoT). The search for lower production cost, shorter production lead time, higher yield of CIS package has becoming more and more challenging. Quality assurance and failure analysis play an important role to ensure high yield production. Typical CIS package failure modes are non-stick on pad (NSOP), lifted CIS die, foreign material on micro lenses, epoxy under cured and stain on cover glass. Most of these failure modes are commonly found in other packages, in this work we highlight on cover glass stain issue which may alter the incoming light intensity and refract its direction and hence producing wrong output signal which is critical when safety of user come into picture especially for automotive industry. The stain observed on cover glass is in white colour with small size, thin layer, low concentration which it difficult to be detected by most of the conventional analysis tools such as Energy Dispersive X-ray (EDX) and Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR). Top surface analysis tools, X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) and Time of Flight Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) were used for the white stain failure analysis. XPS analysis was performed to analyse what is the additional elements present on the white stain as compared to a reference sample, higher Carbon (C) and Oxygen (O) were detected implying that the white stain is likely an organic based material. TOF-SIMS analysis was performed to examine the molecular information of the white stain, fatty acid compound was detected based on 267.3u, 283.3u and 285.3u fragments. Fatty acid is commonly used in die attach epoxy, the white stain on cover glass is likely formed during epoxy process that causes outgassing of volatile fragments.

articleTitle: Failure Analysis on Diode-triggered Silicon-Controlled Rectifiers By using Nondestructive X-ray Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: As the complexity of integrated circuits increases, the electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection devices become critical to reliability issues. However, the physical failure analysis of ESD devices is destructive and time-consuming. In this work, by using the X-ray microscopy (XRM), we study the abnormal change in the leakage current of diode-triggered silicon-controlled rectifiers (DTSCRs) ESD structure under transmission line pulsing stressing. XRM is nondestructive physical failure analysis method by showing the in-depth morphology information of the devices. The results show that the proposed ESD devices have two parts, one is the trigger diodes part and the other is the SCR part. The SCR part was severely damaged and the contact and vias are melted under the electrical stressing, while the trigger diodes part remains intact. The failure analysis is nondestructive, multi-view, and time-saving. It is enlightening the design of novel ESD devices.

articleTitle: Virtual Metrology of Visualizing Copper Microstructure Featured with Computer Vision and Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Virtual metrology of visualizing copper microstructure featured with computer vision and artificial neural network is reported. The focused ion beam images of copper microstructures are modeled. The input is the process variables of fabricating thin copper film and output is the microstructure image corresponding to the process variables. Computer vision and artificial neural network are used to generate model parameters. Images are generated using the model. Nucleation, grains, grain boundaries and twins are all visualized. The features of nucleation and grain growth are quantitatively analyzed in the images. The results of the predicted images support that the inference of microstructure images is proven. The technique is adaptive to most imaging systems and one of the exploratory applications of virtual metrology.

articleTitle: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) of Surface Contamination by TOF-SIMS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Static time of flight secondary ions mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) is a qualitative analysis technique with a high detection limit capable of achieving parts per million (ppm) levels [1] and sub monolayer surface detection. Due to its high sensitivity, the data obtained may contains more than hundreds of peaks including information about sample composition, chemical compound, fragments ions, sample purity, and etc. [2]. Therefore, TOF-SIMS data interpretation is complicated and time consuming especially for unknown contamination. These challenges could be overcome by Principal Component Analysis (PCA). PCA is one of a multivariate method used to identify mass peak spectral in various principal component loadings when processing large data sets such as TOF-SIMS data. This paper presents a study of surface contamination analysis using image based PCA to find out the parent ion of the contaminant.

articleTitle: EBIC Technique Study for Implant Doping Problem in Failure Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Application of Electron Beam Absorbed Current (EBAC) and Electron Beam Induced Current (EBIC) are commonly used in fault localization for open, high resistance, and short failures at the back-end metal layer, and leakage failure in the front-end layer. However, when a device suffers leakage failure caused by improper implant doping problems, EBC technique can help us to precisely diagnose the failure location. In the general analysis of device failure, the device characteristic measurement usually verifies the leakage with the nano-probing instrument, and then verifies the leakage mechanism by cross-section Focused Ion Beam (FIB) or Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) methodologies. However, the physical analysis of implant issue cannot be easily observed by conventional FIB or TEM.In this study, we operate nano-probing to verify the device leakage path from drain to source, and then utilize the principle of Electron Beam Absorbed Current (EBAC) and Electron Beam Induced Current (EBIC) to exactly approach the failure site and successfully demonstrate that the failure mechanism comes from the implant issue which is proved by further Scanning Capacitance Microscopy (SCM) analysis.

articleTitle: In-situ SEM micromechanical experiments on Dual Damascene Copper test structures for investigation of interfacial properties of copper interconnects
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Small-scale delamination experiments at single copper vias in on-chip interconnect stacks of microelectronic chips are performed using a novel experimental setup for testing of interface properties of single copper interconnect structures. The method is based on in-situ SEM nanoindentation experiments, utilized to test customized copper test structures manufactured in the Dual Damascene process. In this unique way, the test structures resemble product-like length-scales as well as material and interface properties. For the investigation of interface properties, the experimental load-displacement data is reviewed. FIB cross sections are performed to validate the delaminated interface. The results gain information on the critical delamination forces and show a good reproducibility for two investigated interfaces. Future work could focus on re-simulating the experimental load-displacement data and thereby gain knowledge of interfacial toughness parameters.

articleTitle: Improving tomographic sensing of Scalpel SPM with multi-probe functionality and automatic removal rate extraction
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: We report on the use of a multi-probe sensing scheme for the implementation of tomographic atomic force microscopy. This leverages the use of three independent probes, alternating their operation on the same area of the sample surface, thus enabling fast tip replacement and high-resolution imaging. Here, two areas of improvement are discussed, namely (1) the development of a synchronized multi-probe sensing method for the accurate control of removed material, and (2), the creation of a data acquisition scheme for the automated extraction of removal rate.

articleTitle: Guidelines of Plasma-FIB Delayering Techniques for Advanced Process Node
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: A precise and reliable technique using plasma focus ion beam (PFIB) to conduct IC chip delayering on sub-16nm technology is proposed. Through a series of DOE (design of experiment), we successfully improve the uniformity by modifying the gas concentration. In addition, geometric effect of MultiChem, and end point monitor system are also discussed to achieve a uniform and accurate delayering result.

articleTitle: Stability of Schottky Barrier Diode Integrated in p-GaN Enhancement-mode GaN Power Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this work, the performance and stability of integrated power Schottky Barrier Diodes (SBD) are reported. We demonstrate the fabrication method to integrate Gated Edge Termination (GET)-SBD into a p-GaN E-mode GaN power technology for 200V power switching applications. The 30mm wide integrated SBDs show a low forward voltage (Vf) and can deliver more than 10A and 6A at V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ac</inf>=3V for 25°C and 150°C, respectively. Furthermore, an on-resistance (Ron) increase of less than 20% up to 200V at 25°C/150°C can be obtained during pulsed IV characterization and OFF-state stress, indicating a promising stability of the integrated GET-SBDs on power p-GaN Gate High Electron Mobility Transistors (HEMTs) platform.

articleTitle: Degradation Studies on 8-Layer 3D Vertical Resistive Random Access Memory Under Moisture
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Resistive random-access memory (RRAM) is a promising alternative to Flash memory. For high density application, 3D vertical RRAM (VRRAM) is a cost-effective method that attracts many attentions. However, the VRRAM also has some reliability issues. In this paper, the degradation under moisture stress is studied. High resistant state(HRS) is sensitive to moisture, while the low resistant state(LRS) remains stable. So, the moisture stress decreases the memory window. This degradation is caused by the moisture invasion HfO2/TaOx interface along the side wall and reduce the barrier of the interface. Based on Poole-Frenkel emission, this paper models the degradation mechanism to illustrate the process.

articleTitle: TEM EELS analysis for DRAM failure analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this work, the electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) methodology was used to dig out the failure mechanism of marginal DRAM electrical failure issues. The EELS spectrum image (SI), energy-loss near-edge structure (ELNES), and MLLS (multiple linear least squares) fitting techniques were utilized to obtain high resolution elemental mappings and chemical bonding information. Three case studies were conducted. In the first case, we successfully used EELS SI and ELNES techniques to find out and identify the TiN extrusion between the storage node contact (SNC) and its neighboring bit line (BL). This leakage path would cause the DRAM retention issue. In the second case, we used the ELNES MLLS fitting method to obtain the Co-silicide phase distribution mapping within NC silicide area. We found the incomplete phase transformation from CoSi to CoSi2 is the root cause of the high resistance path which may lead to a DRAM timing issue. In the last case, we utilized ELNES MLLS techniques to separate Si signals from the overlapped Si3Nx spacer layer and enhance the contrast of the abnormal Si leakage path.

articleTitle: Study of Layout effect on Gate oxide TDDB in sub-16nm FinFET technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this work, TDDB characteristic in sub-16nm FinFET technology are investigated by experiments. The Weibull slope β and voltage coefficient n of NMOSFET and PMOSFET are equals to 1.45/0.95 and -30.5/-37.6 based on the results having various stress voltage, respectively. Moreover, since the layout effect of NMOSFET and PMOSFET, the difference in T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">63</inf> normalized by total device gate oxide area are more than 4X and 2.5X. The dependence between Initial I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> and T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bd</inf> are studied, which shows that there is a negative correlation between initial Ig ratio and T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bd</inf> ratio since difference of the equivalent gate oxide thickness E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ox</inf>. Besides, mean E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ox</inf> of 4Fins device is significantly larger than 2Fins device and 12Fins device based on the results of cumulative probability of the normalized initial I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>, which results in the V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">stress</inf> gain of 4Fins device are equal to 88.5mV and 118.7mV for NMOSFET and PMOSFET, respectively.

articleTitle: Charge–Sensing method for Nickel contamination detection on a 4H-SiC PowerMOSFET
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Process induced contamination became a key point in the recent years to focus the yield improvement on 4H-SiC PowerMOSFET in the production lines. It has been demonstrated that metallic contamination could compromising irreparably transistor performances and reliability. Moreover, the threshold instability is addressed to SiC/SiO2 interface or gate oxide issues. In this work a new method based on charge-sensing to detect intermediate dielectric contamination effect is shown..The confirmation of the hypothesized model has been confirmed by controlled contamination on TEOS layer.

articleTitle: Study on the Factors of Start-up White Line Caused by Coupled Electric Field in TFT LCD
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this paper, we report on the factors of Start-up White Line defect caused by coupled electric field. The defect appeared near the Gate signal line of the display area at zero gray step of the start-up sequence. The failure mechanism was found out to be the coupled electric field caused by the voltage difference between the Common and Gate-Low signals. It affected the charge density in the surrounding Black Matrix and created a new electric field which disturbed the deflection of the liquid crystal. Further experiments and analysis showed that the failure was related to the voltage difference between the common and Gate-Low signals, the resistance of Black Matrix, the pattern of Black Matrix.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Failure in High-Voltage VDMOS Device caused by Die Contamination
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Vertical double diffused metal oxide semiconductor (VDMOS) device is one of the most widely used power semiconductor devices. Multiple VDMOS devices for aerospace application failed after reliability tests. The device function was abnormal because drain-source breakdown voltage (BVDSS) and zero gate voltage leakage current (IDSS) were out of tolerance. Failure analysis and defect localization methods were utilized to determine the root cause of VDMOS failure. The causes of chip leakage were localized and analyzed by means of electrical test, infrared thermographic defect localization, superficial surface microscopic morphology observation, and chemical composition analysis. It was found that there was a small amount of contamination on the chip surface. The contaminant ions migrated into the inner chip, forming an inverted layer at the edge of the chip, and creating additional leakage channels. These factors lead to the chip failure. Compared with the conventional failure analysis method for VDMOS device, the comprehensive failure analysis method proposed in this study can directly locate defect point, observe the morphology of failure area and determine the root cause of failure. Results of the failure analysis provides a basis for improving manufacturing process and device reliability.

articleTitle: Application of EBIC and EBAC for Nanoscale Fault Isolation of FEOL Defect
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The advancement of semiconductor integrated circuit technology demands for nanoscale fault localization techniques to pinpoint the defect location. This is especially critical for subtle front-end of line defects which are easily destroyed from conventional top-down physical delayering or cross-section FIB and would require precise TEM to visualize the defects. In this paper, 3 case studies of nanoscale fault isolation were demonstrated using EBAC/EBIC method to localize the weak point of an ESD implanted clamp transistor design, to isolate the defect that resulted in erase failure in an embedded NVM device and to pinpoint the defect that caused high dark current in PIN SiGe photodiode.

articleTitle: The Monitor and Management of Sulfide Contamination for Probing FAB clean room
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The air-sampling and wafer-sampling analysis procedure of sulfide contamination for circuit probing fab environment was reported due to increasing sensitivity of die level device to contamination. In this investigation, there are three methods used to monitor sulfide-contained species concentration such as the Ag-Si specimen discolored experiment, total sulfur UV-fluorescence analyzer and Ion Chromatography. However, the Ag-Si specimen discolored experiment need OM, SEM and EDS inspection to qualitatively analysis the situation of sulfide contamination. Additionally, the installation of chemical filter was also introduced into the daily facility management system of clean room. All these monitoring procedures and facility engineering approaches are valuable way to prevent the sulfide impact on clean room environment.

articleTitle: Analysis and Improvement of Repeated Wake-up Jittering H-line
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: With the introduction of new concepts such as Industry 4.0, smart manufacturing and smart wearable devices, The TFT-LCD industry has been widely used in all walks of life as the main way for human and computer vision information exchange. Based on the high quality requirements, customers are increasingly demanding verification conditions for their products, which also reveal some problems. This article discusses a type of repetitive wake-up Jittering H-line in the verification process of the customer's complete machine, which is more complicated than the previous jitter stripes. Through the analysis of the defective phenomenon, this topic explores several aspects of the whole system, IC initialization settings, Panel design and TFT characteristics, and conducts simulation based on simulation software to find the cause of the defect and propose effective improvement measures, providing an effective solution for the subsequent new products to circumvent the problem.

articleTitle: Research on the Relationship between the Limit Design and Material of the LGP and the Damage of the LGP
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The limit design and material of the LGP (Light guide plate) in the medium-sized monitor products have a significant impact on the mechanical properties of the module. It is a key design factor to prevent the LGP from being damaged during the fall of the whole machine. Through simulation, theoretical analysis and experiments, the influence of the limit design and material selection of the LGP on the damage of the LGP during the drop of module is studied. It provides a basis for the limit design and material selection of the LGP in the subsequent medium-sized monitor products.

articleTitle: Failure Analysis of Large Area Pt/HfO2/Pt Capacitors Using Multilayer Perceptrons
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this work, we investigated the spatial distribution of failure sites in large area Pt/HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Pt capacitors using simple neural networks as classifiers. When an oxide breakdown (BD) occurs due to severe electrical stress, a mark shows up in the top metal electrode at the location where the failure event took place. The mark is the result of a microexplosion occurring inside the dielectric film. Large area devices need to be studied because the number of generated spots must be the required for statistical analysis. The obtained results using multilayer perceptrons with different number of neurons and hidden layers indicate that the largest breakdown spots tend to concentrate towards the center of the device. This observation is consistent with previous exploratory analysis carried out using spatial statistics techniques. This exercise shows the suitability of multilayer perceptrons for investigating the distribution of failure sites or defects on a given surface.

articleTitle: Digital and AMS Yield Diagnosis Flow Combining Automated Testing and Fault Injection-based Circuit Simulation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This paper proposes an approach to recreate an ATE test shmoo using fault injection-based circuit simulation for the purpose of failure debug. This is achieved through the identification of critical simulation conditions and then assigning an appropriate pass/ fail criterion to the simulation outcome. Through a comparison between the technical and actual failing shmoo, possible failing suspects can be postulated to guide further failure analysis to reveal the root cause. Such approach is particularly useful for failures that are marginal in nature and does not exhibit outlier fail symptoms. Results presented substantiate its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Sample Preparation For VCSEL Device Contamination Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: VCSEL is a vertical cavity surface emitting lasers and any contamination happening on its emitting surface would have severe effect on its lasing performance. Usually, the size of the contamination from either process failure analysis (FA), board reliability or customer return FA is in the micrometer range, and due to its device surface structure, direct application of surface analysis techniques would be rather difficult. In this paper, we proposed and demonstrated a combined technique which uses the focused ion beam (FIB) to prepare a milled contaminant slice from the VCSEL emitting surface, following by the time-of-flight mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) analysis. Therefore, the contamination is able to be determined and identified as possibly coming from carbonyl compound.

articleTitle: Nano-CT imaging of electrically stressed power device metallization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this paper, we show that nano-CT imaging can provide detailed information on the degradation that occurs in power device metallization during a fast PTC stress. Nano-CT imaging provides a high resolution, 3D imaging method to understand degradation mechanisms in packaged power semiconductor devices.

articleTitle: Physical Mechanism for Different Phases and Turn-Around of Idsat in PMOS under HCI Stress
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: It is well known that when PMOS is stressed at I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bmax</inf> or I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gmax</inf>, its I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf> will first increase and then decrease, known as the turn-around effect [1],[7]. In this paper, we will first explain the differences in I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf> changes in the three stress modes of PMOS (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bmax</inf>, I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gmax</inf>, V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>=V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>), then compare the difference between I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf> increase percentages under I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bmax</inf> and I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gmax</inf> stress. Secondly, in regards to the significant increase of I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf> percentage under I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gmax</inf> stress, the results of this paper is seldom mentioned in other papers, such as the appearance of I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gmax</inf> peak in relation to V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>, and I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dlin</inf> always having an earlier turn-around compared to I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf>. Finally, we discuss the occurring time and saturation percentage of I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>'s turn-around at I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gmax</inf> stress with different geometric factors, especially in its correlation with the narrow width effect [5]. The results show, i) the holes tunneling into the oxide near the source side by ΔV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gs</inf> and the hot electrons (generated by HC impact) injecting into the oxide near the drain side by ΔV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gd</inf> compete with each other, bringing about the different I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf> changes of the three stress modes; ii) the horizontal and vertical electric fields affect the impact point of HCI and the peak point (the highest probability) of the hot electrons injecting into the oxide (we abbreviated as PPHEIIO), effecting the larger increase of I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf> percentage under I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gmax</inf> stress compared to I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bmax</inf> stress. This brief explanation is seldom mentioned in other papers; lastly, the energy carried by the holes and the channel lattice scattering affect the energy of the hot electrons, which affected the turn-around effect for PMOS stressed at I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gmax</inf>. At the same time, besides "interplay between interface trap generation and trapping of carriers by oxide traps" mentioned by other papers being the only explanation for earlier turn-around of I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dlin</inf> as to I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf>, the increase in R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf> seems to be an important influencing factor.

Author Keywords: PPHEIIO (peak point of hot electrons injection into the oxide)

articleTitle: Rapid Assessment of Semiconductor Thermal Quality
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The performance and reliability of an IC Package will be affected by die attach defects such as voids, cracks and delaminations. In this paper, a novel Thermal Quality Tester is presented. It allows for non-intrusive and non-destructive tests of the samples within a very short period of time. Thermal transient tests are used to determine the thermal impedance and structure function curves of the samples. The samples can then be binned according to their thermal performance. Thermal simulations of the samples are used to provide information for the binning process. The concepts for this tester will be presented along with test sample measurements.

articleTitle: A Systematic Failure Analysis Approach on Copper Pad Discoloration Issue
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Electronic devices are playing a key role in modern electronic products which have energy efficiency features. The electronic devices are required to have good adhesion with wire bonds during the back-end process. Therefore, discoloration on the source pad will lead to higher resistance and poor adhesion during the wire bonding process and can be caused by delamination or crack issues. Thus, the source pad discoloration issue needs to be minimized. This paper outlines the systematic approach of physical analysis to investigate the discoloration issue on copper source pads. The failure analysis revealed copper pad surface discoloration caused by void/crater with depth penetration ~600nm and secondary defect with of higher O element at the affected area. In this paper, the author introduced a physical analysis approach using Auger Electron Spectroscopy (AES) and Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) for the copper pad discoloration issue.

articleTitle: MIPI RFFE functional leakage failure debug using an integrated NI-PXIe setup
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: As communication networks progress into 5G and mmWave spectrum, modern RF systems have become highly sophisticated with multiple high-performance RF front-end modules integrated within. MIPI RFFE protocol defines the standard for configuring, communicating with and also testing the RF front-end modules. Therefore, proficiency in MIPI protocol and being able to manipulate the test patterns plays a significant role in failure characterization and debug. Conventional static debug approach of biasing the power, ground and relevant control pins is not fruitful anymore. On the other hand, setting up of probe card and tester based dynamic fault isolation capabilities is also not a cost-effective solution for RFFE leakage failures due to their low pin count and frequency requirements. In this paper, a semi-dynamic approach is adopted by integrating National Instruments’ PXIe system to either a manual bench station for testing or a static fault isolation system for debugging RFFE functional leakage failures. Segmented pattern analysis has been demonstrated to be effective in failure validation and failure characterization. This paper describes two case studies where NI-PXIe setup together with detailed MIPI protocol understanding led to successful debug of low yield and new product prototype MIPI leakage failures.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning to Reduce Failures in SOT-MRAM Switching
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: We demonstrate the use of reinforcement learning for achieving efficient switching schemes for a field-free operation of spin-orbit torque magnetoresistive random access memory cells. A cell is switched purely electrically by applying two orthogonal current pulses. It is shown that using a reinforcement learning approach, a neural network model can be trained on a fixed material parameter set for finding optimal switching pulse sequences. This model is not only suitable to switch a memory cell in the presence of thermal fluctuations, but also for varied cell material parameters.

articleTitle: Comparison of DC/AC Hot Carrier Degradation between Short Channel Si Bulk and SiGe SOI p-FinFETs
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this study, both direct current (DC) and alternating current (AC) hot carrier degradation (HCD) of Si Bulk p-FinFETs and SiGe SOI p-FinFETs with 40 nm channel length are compared. The time exponent (n), activation energy (EA) and voltage acceleration factor (VAF) under different HCD stress conditions are investigated. Experiments show that DC HCD of Si FinFETs is almost 1.2 times of that of SiGe FinFETs at room temperature. However, SiGe SOI FinFETs are more sensitive to AC signal frequency than Si Bulk FinFETs in AC HCD measurement. With AC frequency increasing, oxide traps capture in AC HCD of SiGe FinFETs is becoming dominant due to the reduction of slow-interface traps capture.

articleTitle: The influence of adhesive tape on L0 light leakage of TFT-LCD products after reliability test
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: L0 light leakage often happens to TFT-LCD products after reliability test. The deformation of the backlight unit has a significant effect on L0 light leakage. The level of backlight deformation transferred to panel directly affects the level of L0 light leakage. This paper analyzes the causes of angle leakage, simulates the effect of different base material tape on stress and deformation of panel, and changes the base material for physical verification, reveals the relationship between tape characteristics and L0 light leakage, and provides a basis for the selection of adhesive tape for TFT-LCD products.

articleTitle: Simple Methods to Improve the CSAM Thru-Scan Efficiency on Package Units
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: CSAM analysis is one of the widely used non-destructive FA techniques. When the CSAM thru-scan mode is needed for a large number of package units, the current tray scan feature may not meet the needs due to its limitations. In this paper, we introduced some simple methods to overcome these limitations under different scenarios, in order to improve the CSAM thru-scan inspection throughput and efficiency. The solutions are proved to be successful and can be applied to similar occasions, especially for those irregular units.

articleTitle: NAND Flash Relationship Between the Initial State of Non-Volatile Memory Cycling Endurance and the High Temperature Data Retention Ability of Post Cycling
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Post Cycling High Temperature Data Retention (PCHTDR) is one of the critical stress driven qualification tests specified by JEDEC47 item 5.5 [1] standard to ensure Non-Volatile Memory (NVM) reliability. However, prior to PCHTDR qualification, NVM devices have to undergo cycling endurance test followed by high temperature retention bake. This extensive NVM reliability flow is laborious and time consuming as the device NVM density increases. In this paper, NVM parameters before cycling endurance test and after PCHTDR test were studied carefully. It was interestingly observed that ICs with high post cycling failure bits exhibited wider initial Vth (threshold voltage) bandwidth distribution and slower page program time. The slow program time causes serious tunnel oxide damage after cycling that induces PCHTDR Vth drop amount huge and PCHTDR fail bit rate (FBR) higher after baking.

articleTitle: E-test Probe Mark Topology-induced Failure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this paper, we show evidence of a unique failure at wafer sort that is caused by inline E-test probing on scribe line structures. This happens in spite of a safe probe distance from the prime die and the presence of typical seal ring surrounding chip periphery. Experimental results to relate probe marks topology created from mechanical probing on copper pads to sort outcome are presented. We discuss the failure mechanism and prove that probecard design and control is critical to avoid such fails.

articleTitle: Meticulous system calibration as a key for extracting correct photon emission spectra
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Photon Emission (PE) spectra have been investigated for decades in order to extract important data of device failures or characteristic parameters. InGaAs detectors are more problematic than Si detectors because of their more pronounced noise behaviour. Many published results of spectral analysis performed with InGaAs detectors have not been fully conclusive. With a principal approach as to which spectra can be expected from digital ICs in PE, the shape of the measured spectra did not always correspond to these fundamental principles. This paper shows that a meticulous calibration of a spectral photon emission microscopy (SPEM) setup is the key to extracted PE spectra that correspond to the theoretical basics. Furthermore, a concept for the implementation of a thorough calibration procedure is given and several errors that may occur during this procedure as well as their influence on spectral analyses are discussed. Finally, the parameter electron temperature of the field effect transistor (FET) can be successfully extracted from InGaAs based spectra.

articleTitle: Failure Analysis and Reliability Improvement of the Corner Region of Variation Lateral Doping Termination
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Experiments showed that the power MOSFET devices with the variation lateral doping (VLD) termination were prone to fail in the corner regions, for the lower effective dopant concentration in the corner areas of the VLD termination makes it vulnerable to burn out there. By solving the three-dimensional Poisson equation, an optimal distribution of doping concentration in the corner region is deduced. The electric field intensity in the corner region is reduced with the optimized doping profile. Meanwhile, the reliability problems caused by the curvature effect is relieved. The VLD termination designed by proposed analytical model has higher breakdown voltage and lower failure rate compared to the conventional structure.

articleTitle: Analyze the ESD Performance and Bandwidth Difference for LC T-Network and Bridged T-Coil
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The bridged T–coil circuit (BTC) and the LC T-network are well known matching circuits. These circuits are differentiated only by the bridged capacitor (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf>). The two circuits have same electrostatic-discharge (ESD) performance while their bandwidths are different. Based on the complex conjugate matching theorem, the component relation model of the BCT and the LC T-network are derived in this paper. From the derivation, the bandwidth extension mechanism of the BTC is revealed as the C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf> can equalize the coefficient of each power of s for all impedances or admittances of BTC to make them synchronize with frequency to cancel out at any frequency.

articleTitle: Temperature Cycling Failure Analysis and Improvement of A Panel Level Fan-out QFN Package
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This article analyzed the temperature cycling test failure root cause and molding film crack mechanism of a panel level fan-out QFN package. Improvement actions are proposed according to Kitagawa-Takahashi diagram. In the micro crack stage, reducing the thermal stress is the key point. As the crack dimension grows to the macro crack propagation stage, crack propagation threshold and SIF must be well balanced. In addition, the maximum non-propagation crack length is also a key factor to optimize the crack issue. These factors are strongly related to material properties such as CTE and Young’s modules. Detail improvement actions are advised by finite element analysis method and verified through experiments. The optimized products have passed TC1000 cycles reliability test with crack free.

articleTitle: SIMS Methodology Study of Indium Implant Quantification
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) is typically used for implantation depth profiling and dosage quantification. Energy filtering approach is commonly used to eliminate the mass interference caused by the molecular ions of Si [1]. However, it is accompanied by a severe loss of the measurement precision of dosage and therefore it is not suitable for low dosage (E+13 at/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) indium implant quantification. In this paper, SIMS analysis by 2 types of test method – with and without voltage offset will be discussed to decide a more appropriate approach of low dose indium implant sample evaluation.

articleTitle: Failure Analysis on MIM capacitor failures of RF devices using simple circuit edit passive voltage contrast method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Failure analysis in radio frequency (RF) devices are becoming more increasingly complex and challenging with the scaling of technology. One of the most commonly used passive components in analog and mixed-signal devices is the metal-insulator-metal (MIM) capacitors [1]. Failure analysis (FA) in such capacitors is challenging. In our previous paper, we introduced and applied a simple circuit edit passive voltage contrast (CE-PVC) technique in failure analysis [2]. This technique uses a conventional scanning electron microscope (SEM) and platinum deposition that is readily available in most labs SEM to manipulate passive voltage contrasts through minor, reversible circuit editing. In this paper, this technique was further expanded to resolve MIM structure failures on RF devices. This paper successfully demonstrated and resolved two different failures, open-related and short defects with the CE-PVC technique.

articleTitle: Metal Migration Induced Breakdown from Gate Contact in Bulk FinFET Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Bulk fin field-effect transistor (FinFET) devices with excellent gate control ability are promising to succeed the planar devices under Moore’s law. With the scaling down of the feature size, the reliability of the FinFET device becomes an urgent issue. Also, the miniaturized three-dimensional structure of bulk FinFET makes the failure characterization more challenging. In this paper, we carried out the direct current (DC) breakdown and transmission line pulse (TLP) breakdown in the bulk FinFET. Corresponding microstructural and chemical elements’ differences between gate contact and gate electrode are characterized by transmission electron microscopy (TEM). For both experiments, the fin nearest to gate contact is completely damaged under electrical stressing. The destruction of DC is more serious, which has a large area fusion with metal migration. The TLP damage is local and tends to form a void. The gate contact structure is intact with slight elements’ migration. This work paves a guideline for the reliability improvements of FinFET.

articleTitle: TEM-EDX Characterization of Immersion Pd & Pd-MoOx on Cu & NiP
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Immersion palladium (Pd) alloyed with molybdenate (MoOx) is developed and coated on copper (Cu) to reduce the Cu diffusion into Pd. The level of Cu diffusion was compared with immersion Pd. The Pd and Pd-MoOx layer coated on top of Cu and the layers’ interface are characterized using Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) and Energy Dispersive X-ray (EDX) line scan. Approximate 55 - 60 atomic% of Cu diffusion into the Pd layer is observed for immersion Pd (70 nm) coating on Cu. While immersion Pd-MoOx provides a Pd layer of 37nm thickness with less Cu diffusion (appx. 40%). Immersion Pd and Pd-MoOx were also performed on sample with electroless nickel phosphorous (NiP) layer. Significant crystalline structure of immersion Pd layer with approx. 45nm thickness is observed. The grain size of crystalline structure of Pd-MoOx (58 nm) on NiP is smaller compared to the one of Pd only. With the integration of MoOx and oxide into the Pd layer, it is expected that the density of the film will be greatly reduced. Finally, the NiP samples coated with Pd and Pd-MoOx were dipped into immersion gold (Au) solution for 10 minutes respectively, where both samples show Au thickness of approximately 70 nm, with no black pad (phosphorous left over) are observed. Immersion Pd and Pd-MoOx can be used to prevent black pad during Au plating on NiP. In this case, immersion Pd-MoOx utilize less Pd (lower cost) compared to immersion Pd for this purpose.

articleTitle: Research on the design factors affecting the COG Mura of IPS display products
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The root cause of COG Mura is analyzed and the main influencing factors in design are determined through theoretical analysis, simulation and experiment. A set of systematic theoretical design guidelines is proposed, and it has been applied to many product designs and processes afterwards.

articleTitle: Silicon Defect Observation From Ultra-Thick Sample Using TEM EELS Technique
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this paper, we have applied an uncommon transmission electron microscopy (TEM) technique to observe silicon defects from an ultra-thick (> 3um) bulk specimen. This method combines TEM with the electron-energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) technique. Using this technique, we were able to observe the presence of large size silicon defects that formed deep across the wafer. Compared with the conventional TEM method, this technique provides a more complete profile of the silicon defect and is useful in identifying the root cause of the defect formation. In addition, the success rate of capturing the defect is higher due to much larger specimen thickness is used.

articleTitle: Failure Mechanism of Stress Migration in Via Sidewall for Dual Damascene Cu Interconnection
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Generally, as devices scale, Cu metal is used more in the dual damascene process structure due to its better conductivity. TaN/Ta was often used because of better adhesion to Cu and SiO2, which are used as a barrier layer between IMD and Cu metal. SM is the phenomenon of metal void under tension of thermal stress. When the stress migration test (SM) was performed at three kinds of baking temperatures (150,200,250 °C ), it was only found that the minimum metal line width connected with the Via, SIV (stress induced voids) phenomenon will occur in via-1 sidewall at a temperature of 250°C.This paper will discuss the CDF plot results of SM and failure mechanisms, which were based on relative experiments such as via hole aspect ratio (AR) adjustment, Via bottom profile adjustment, SiCN remain thickness adjustment, polymer residue and barrier coverage improvement items.
